images.title: The crane and the four little chicks
images.purpose: Set the story of the opener in front of the student: a Siberian Crane and four little chicks flying over the land, with a compass that shows the four directions, and no explanation.
images.composition: Over two hills, one large white crane at the left leads four small yellow chicks in a loose line to the right, all flying to the left; a compass card sits in the top right corner.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816, flat colours, thin dark #2B2B2B outlines (3 px). LANDSCAPE at the bottom, two hills and nothing else: the far hill is a wide rounded hill filled grey #6B7280, an ellipse centred at x 1000 and y 816 with half width 600 and half height 260, so its top is at y 556, cut off by the right edge and the bottom edge of the frame; the near hill is a rounded hill filled green #009E73, an ellipse centred at x 340 and y 816 with half width 620 and half height 190, so its top is at y 626, cut off by the left edge and the bottom edge, and it stands in front of the far hill. No trees, no houses, no water, no Sun, no clouds. BIRDS in the air above the hills, five in all and every one flying towards the left of the frame: ONE Siberian Crane and FOUR chicks. THE CRANE, side view, in the left part of the frame, with a white body (an ellipse 220 by 90 px, centre x 480 and y 330, white fill), a long white neck stretched forward to the left and slightly up (a curved band 28 px thick from the left end of the body at x 380 up to y 285 at x 270), a small white head at the end of the neck (a circle 44 px wide, centre x 250 and y 280) with ONE long straight beak pointing left (a thin triangle 60 px long, red #D55E00), a red #D55E00 patch on the face round the eye (a circle 22 px wide) and one small dark #1F2937 eye dot; TWO wings spread upwards and backwards from the body, the near wing a long curved wing shape reaching from x 470 up to y 150 and back down to x 640 with its outer third filled dark #1F2937 as the black wing tips and the rest white, and the far wing a smaller wing of the same kind behind it reaching up to y 190; TWO long thin legs trailing straight back to the right (two lines 6 px thick, grey #6B7280, from x 580 to x 760, at y 340 and y 352); and ONE short white tail (a small triangle 50 px long) at the right end of the body. THE FOUR CHICKS follow the crane in a loose zigzag line to the right, all facing left, all exactly the same size and drawn the same way: a round body (an ellipse 90 by 60 px) filled amber #E69F00, a round head (a circle 44 px wide) of the same amber at the front left of the body, a small red #D55E00 beak (a triangle 18 px long) pointing left, one dark #1F2937 eye dot, and one small white wing on the body (a teardrop 40 by 24 px). Chick centres: chick 1 at x 840 and y 290, chick 2 at x 960 and y 370, chick 3 at x 1080 and y 290, chick 4 at x 1200 and y 370. COMPASS CARD in the top right corner: a square card with rounded corners (corner radius 16 px), 200 by 200 px, from x 1196 to x 1396 and from y 36 to y 236, white fill, dark #2B2B2B outline 6 px. Inside it, a cross of two thin double headed dark arrows (4 px thick): one vertical from y 106 to y 176 at x 1296 and one horizontal from x 1262 to x 1332 at y 141. The letter N in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (44 px) centred at x 1296 and y 80 (top), the letter S in dark bold centred at x 1296 and y 200 (bottom), the letter W in dark bold centred at x 1226 and y 141 (left) and the letter E in red #D55E00 bold centred at x 1368 and y 141 (right). In all: 1 crane, 4 chicks, 2 hills, 1 compass card. No other text, no numbers, no title. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: A Siberian Crane and four little chicks fly over the land, and the compass shows the four directions the poem names.
images.description: A white Siberian Crane and four small yellow chicks flying to the left over two hills, with a compass card in the top right corner.
images.context: Concept image for the hook, Four Little Chicks and the Siberian Crane. It draws the opener of your maths book, the crane that flies from Siberia and the four little chicks of the poem, with the compass rose, and it explains nothing about how birds find their way.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student look at the birds and the compass and wonder how a bird, or a person, keeps track of directions. Say no answer: your maths book does not explain how birds find their path, so it stays a question to wonder about. The slip to watch: taking the picture as a fact about bird journeys when it only sets the story.

image_decisions.why: The crane, the four little chicks and the compass put the story and the four directions in front of the student before any rule is said, which words alone cannot do.
